chunking: single wave — 3075-line diff is within the ~3000 tolerance (+2.5%, driven by 2021 lines of generated golden data; ~1050 reviewable lines); every lens reviewed identical bytes

local_suite.harness_run: 25/25 demos green (24 pre-existing goldens unshifted; pause new)
local_suite.perkins_data_audit: goldens/pause.t1 window 1211..1400 = one repeated hash (0xd3600eef9503b6d9), hash moves exactly at 1401; pause.log.bin decodes: mid-pause draw logged at apply_tick 1211 (paused tick 1210+1), no-pause draws at back-compat floor+1 (=3)

findings.title: Pause-schedule parsing checks file-order alternation but not chronological at_ms order — an inverted/out-of-order pause+resume pair silently cancels or inverts the window and u64-underflows ticks_stepped_by
findings.evidence: parse: `if last_pause != -1 && last_pause == 1 { return ..., "pause schedule must alternate (two pauses in a row)" }` — file order only. run.odin: `hi := min(wall_tick, re - 1); n -= hi - pe + 1` with re from the NEXT non-paused event in slice order regardless of at_ms.
findings.detail: `at 70000ms pause` then `at 60500ms resume` passes arity+alternation; paused_at's last-wins loop never pauses (the pause silently vanishes); ticks_stepped_by underflows (hi-pe+1 negative in u64) so commands fired at >= the pause ms get garbage apply_ticks silently logged into a blessed log.
findings.recommended_fix: At parse time reject a pause/resume whose at_ms is <= the previous pause event's at_ms (track last_pause_ms alongside last_pause) — the same fail-loud standard as the alternation check; optionally clamp the window subtraction.

findings.title: Save/bless path ignores the pause-window stability violations it detects — contradicts the code's own 'fail loud, never bless a broken pause' contract
findings.location: harness/run.odin:333-339 (violation appended to fails) + 420-425 (save branch returns true without inspecting fails)
findings.evidence: Paused branch: `} else if hashes[len(hashes)-1] != pause_base { append(&fails, fmt.aprintf("paused state STABLE violation at wall tick %d...")) }` ... save branch: `if save { write_manifest(...); write_file(log_path(name), ...); fmt.printf("  save ..."); return true }`
findings.detail: A drifting paused window still gets blessed by `harness save` (fails never checked, not even printed in save mode). Run-mode catches drift; the deliberate re-bless path silently accepts a broken pause — exactly the class of silent-bless the in-code comment promises can't happen.
findings.recommended_fix: In the save branch, fail the save (print fails, return false) when len(fails) > 0 — mirror the replay_error check that already gates save.

findings.title: core/pause_test clause (a) pins boundary hash-equality (wall-11 == wall-10) that the real harness contract explicitly disavows — holds only because the fixture emits zero events at the pause tick
findings.location: core/pause_test.odin:80-84 vs harness/run.odin:317-322 (the KNOWN-LEGIT boundary comment) and goldens/pause.t1 (boundary hashes differ: df8424... -> d3600e...)
findings.evidence: test: `for w in u64(11)..=20 { testing.expectf(t, live_hashes[w-1] == live_hashes[9], "pause window must be stable at wall tick %d ...") }`; harness comment: "The boundary hash legitimately differs from the last STEPPED tick's hash (that one included the tick's own events)".
findings.detail: state_hash folds the tick's events (core/serialize.odin:66), so wall-11 == wall-10 requires tick 10 to be event-silent — a fixture accident (the golden's boundary tick 1210 emits crisis events, hence differs). A legit fixture change emitting an event at the pause tick would falsely fail the test, and the pin misdocuments the contract as boundary-equality instead of window-internal stability.
findings.recommended_fix: Assert the window against its own first hash (live_hashes[10] as baseline) like the harness does, not against the last stepped tick's hash; keep the (b)/(c)/(d) pins unchanged.

findings.title: New parse-time rejection paths (bad arity, double-pause, resume-without-pause) have zero automated coverage
findings.evidence: No harness/*_test.odin exists; no test invokes parse_demo with an invalid pause schedule. The repo's own standard (harness/drift.odin): "the gate's 'rejects drift' must be PROVEN in CI, not just asserted locally".
findings.detail: The review-r1 hardening claims fail-loud validation, but nothing proves the rejections fire — a future refactor could silently drop them (the exact W1 class of regression would go unnoticed).
findings.recommended_fix: Add a small parse-rejection test set (or a harness self-test verb) covering the three new rejections plus the out-of-order case from W1.

findings.title: apply_tick_at's trailing-pause and multiple-window branches are never exercised
findings.evidence: demos/pause.dem has one non-trailing window (resume at 70000ms, run to 100000ms); core/pause_test uses one non-trailing window (10,20] over 40 ticks. The `re: u64 = max(u64)` trailing branch and multi-window accumulation have no exercised instance.
findings.detail: The lowering's O(len(pauses)) hardening (the 68s-stall fix) is only proven on the single-window shape; trailing/multi-window arithmetic (where the W1 underflow lives) is untested.
findings.recommended_fix: Extend core/pause_test (or a second demo) with a trailing-pause and a two-window case pinning ticks_stepped_by/apply_tick_at outcomes.

findings.title: Paused-state STABLE violation checks (live + replay) are never proven to bite
findings.evidence: drift.odin's seven mutation classes (catalog_hash, logic_hz, bad_magic, bad_version, bad_tag, bad_era, truncated) never mutate apply_tick bytes or the pause schedule; no test forces a mid-window hash move.
findings.detail: The loud stability check — the core tripwire of the 'paused state stable' golden — has no negative test; if its condition were inverted or dropped, every gate would still pass.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a drift class (or unit harness) that shifts the mid-pause edit's apply_tick into the window and asserts the STABLE violation fires in both paths.

findings.title: Advisory test gate: CONCERNS
findings.evidence: P0 (determinism spine: freeze/resume/exact-tick/replay/edit-lowering) fully pinned by pause.dem T1 + replay gate + core/pause_test + drift-check; P1 hardening branches (W4-W6) uncovered.
findings.detail: P0 100%, P1 ~80-85%, overall >80% — CONCERNS per gate thresholds.
findings.recommended_fix: Close W4-W6 (negative tests for the new hardening) to lift the gate to PASS.

findings.title: [downgraded from warning] Pause toggle's else-branch maps ANY non-Run mode to Run — unreachable today (mode is only Run/Paused at that point)
findings.evidence: `app.mode = .Paused if app.mode == .Run else .Run` — start_run sets mode = Run before the loop (line 302); Game_Over returns early (line 330); Boot never reaches handle_input.
findings.detail: Latent only: no reachable path evaluates the else with Boot/Game_Over. A future mode added to the FSM would silently toggle into Run though.
findings.recommended_fix: Optionally gate the toggle on (mode == .Run || mode == .Paused) for explicitness.

findings.title: Paused veil rect uses live window size but the PAUSED label centers on WIN_W/WIN_H constants
findings.detail: After a resize the veil covers the full window but the label stays at the 1280x720 center — off-center label. Corner-anchored HUD text shares the fixed-coord convention, but this is the first centered element.
findings.recommended_fix: Center the label on GetScreenWidth/Height (or track live size in draw_text's helper).

findings.title: pause.dem comment (and PR body) claim the crisis banner's 'countdown' is where the pause left it — the banner renders no countdown
findings.evidence: draw_crisis_banner renders title + static preventive_redesign hint only (app/render/crisis.odin:58-75, no tick-derived text); by 80000ms the sim legitimately advanced 200 post-resume ticks.
findings.detail: The T2 pair does prove the crisis is still active with a pixel-identical banner strip; the 'countdown exactly where paused' phrasing overstates what the banner shows.
findings.recommended_fix: Reword to 'the same crisis still active, banner pixel-identical; the window advanced only post-resume (none during the pause)'.

findings.title: The pause-aware virtual-clock loop + stability check is triplicated (run_demo, replay_hashes, core/pause_test's record_paused_run)
findings.evidence: All three carry the same paused-branch/baseline/stability structure with slight variations (allocator discipline differs in the replay copy).
findings.detail: Three hand-kept copies of the determinism-critical loop; a future change must land in all three or the paths diverge (the ODN-11 lesson the Demo_Replay struct itself codifies).
findings.recommended_fix: Extract a shared virtual-clock step driver (harness) the test can also drive; keep the test's copy only if independence is the goal — then document that.

findings.title: pause_effect_tick's i64 multiply wraps for absurd at_ms — pre-existing convention extended to pause events
findings.evidence: `return u64(max(0, i64(p.at_ms) * i64(logic_hz) / 1000)) + 1` — at_ms > ~4.6e17 wraps negative, clamps to 0, effect = 1.
findings.detail: Identical arithmetic to the pre-5.3 command lowering (intent_apply_tick_raw); new code copies the convention rather than introducing a new hazard. Demo files are in-repo authored artifacts.
findings.recommended_fix: If ever hardened, validate at_ms bounds at parse time for all at-directives at once.
